0.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_000
0.description: The road ahead of you is long and perilous, but should you reach the laboratory's thirtieth floor, you shall be as well versed in its workings as any of the researchers who once toiled within its halls.

1.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_001
1.description: I would be concerned if you were anyone else, but I have the utmost confidence that your valor will see you through. Of course, I expect─and very much look forward to─a full report of your findings.

2.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_010
2.description: Your expedition has given even this ancient soul a long-forgotten sense of purpose.

3.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_011
3.description: You deserve a reward, and I have ever considered knowledge to be the most precious resource of all. So, ask me aught of the creatures and experiments you have encountered in Eureka Orthos, and I shall furnish you with what I know of their workings.

4.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_012
4.description: Hoho! I understand you have been quite busy. The better part of Eureka Orthos's hidden hallways now bear the mark of your footsteps─a boast that not even I could make!

5.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_013
5.description: However, I caution you to not let your better judgment be clouded by pride. Eureka Orthos is a tomb for the secrets of Allag, and I would hate to see you buried amongst that detritus.

6.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_014
6.description: Koh has withdrawn inside herself, seemingly content to listen rather than speak. I see little reason to gainsay her decision.

7.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_015
7.description: Such are the choices one must make when sharing a vessel. I have an obligation to fulfill to you, besides, so if there are any questions burning a hole in your mind, you have the full cooperation of Archmagus Noah.

15.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_032
15.description: Tell me about Doga and Unei.

17.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_034
17.description: Tell me about Gancanagh on floor 10.

18.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_035
18.description: Tell me about the cloning system on floor 20.

19.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_036
19.description: Tell me about the clone of Tiamat on floor 30.

20.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_037
20.description: Tell me about the clone of Twintania on floor 40.

21.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_038
21.description: Tell me about the servomechanical chimera 14X on floor 50.

22.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_039
22.description: Tell me about the servomechanical minotaur 16 on floor 60.

23.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_040
23.description: Tell me about the aeturna on floor 70.

24.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_041
24.description: Tell me about Proto-Kaliya on floor 80.

25.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_042
25.description: Tell me about the Administrator on floor 90.

26.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_A2_000_043
26.description: Tell me about Excalibur on floor 99.

28.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_050
28.description: The tomestone inserted into Excalibur's storage unit contains detailed records on the weapon in question.

29.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_051
29.description: I realize that the adventurers of today care little for such dry records aside from where market value is concerned, but that is your own fault for not knowing how to use them.

30.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_052
30.description: Fortunately, it was a simple matter for me to program the synthesis node to import the design elements recorded therein, and the resulting Excalibur-themed accoutrements should suffice to pique your interest. The weapon was a true work of art, after all.

31.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_SYSTEM_000_053
31.description: You can exchange Orthos tomestones for four types of accessories by presenting them to the synthesis node.

32.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_SYSTEM_000_054
32.description: If you speak to Koh Rabntah with all four of these accessories equipped or in your inventory, you will earn an achievement and a rare item.

33.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_055
33.description: I have something to give you, but...gods, <hex:02080FE905FF06776F6D616EFF046D616E03>, must you carry an entire arsenal in your pack? I would hate for your illustrious career to be cut short by a bad back.

34.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_SYSTEM_000_056
34.description: To collect your reward, ensure you have sufficient inventory space and speak with Koh Rabntah once more.

35.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_057
35.description: You are quite full of surprises, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. It was impressive enough that you conquered every corner of Eureka Orthos, but that you would brave those halls yet again is truly remarkable! Indeed you know naught of fear.

36.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_058
36.description: And you have benefited from your own bravery, it seems. The data from the tomestones you recovered proved sufficient to synthesize a complete set of breathtaking accessories.

37.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_059
37.description: Now, Excalibur's beauty is the proverbial feather in your cap! You deserve it, for scarcely in my long years have I seen such a passion for discovery.

38.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_060
38.description: Since you leapt into the jaws of danger at my behest, I feel it is my duty to reward you for your thoroughness.

39.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_061
39.description: Although the debt I owe cannot be paid by material goods, I hope this aeturna I came across in an experimental vat will provide some measure of satisfaction. It <hex:021A020203>appears<hex:021A020103> to be friendly.

40.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_062
40.description: If left in the facility, its fate would have been a short life of loneliness and drudgery. But now, with you, it has many long years of derring-do ahead of it!

41.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_070
41.description: Myself? Surprisingly, 'tis not a question I hear often... Truth be told, I find it difficult to know where to begin.

42.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_071
42.description: Perhaps with the empire? When Allag was at the height of its prosperity─and indolence─I was hailed as the greatest magus that had ever lived. Wealth and fame came as easily to me as death and taxes come to the common lot.

43.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_072
43.description: I do not boast, you can be sure─I truly was the greatest. Even Amon's considerable talents were as a sputtering candle when placed next to my brilliance. When it came to magical aptitude, in any case.

44.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_073
44.description: As the empire's luminary, admirers and patrons alike vied for my attention. I was free to sate my boundless curiosity and pursue untold strength. In each and every way, I lived a full life.

45.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_074
45.description: Even the severance of my soul from my body was a natural consequence of these pursuits. By doing so, I thrust myself outside of time's creeping reach, escaping the ravages of age.

46.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_075
46.description: Alas, I could not do the same for Allag. As the years passed, cracks began to form in the empire's foundation.

47.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_076
47.description: As the rebels descended upon the empire to put their wounded prey out of its misery, I set my sights forward to the civilizations waiting in the years ahead.

48.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_077
48.description: Would chaos and disorder come crawling over the horizon? Or would peace and prosperity find purchase, banishing all strife from the world? I sought a place far below that would suit my reverie, and there did I seal myself away.

49.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_078
49.description: To think that it would be Amon's magicks that propelled me across the eons and into this era. Well, at least I shall never lack for stories of high adventure with which to bore my pupils.

50.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_080
50.description: Ah, I take it you found data concerning the siblings in your expedition.

51.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_081
51.description: I should not be surprised. The pair were extremely cooperative when it came to research on cloning technology, even offering themselves up as subjects.

52.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_082
52.description: The direct support of the royal family spurred progress by leaps and bounds. Xande's resurrection was a direct result of Unei and Doga's contributions. The feat could not have been achieved without his direct descendants.

53.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_083
53.description: And there was more. The control system that used royal blood as a key arose from the multitude of clones produced from the siblings.

54.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_084
54.description: Doubtless this solidified the emperor's role as the beacon of Allag, making his authority unassailable. It also must have put to rest any number of courtly intrigues and disputes over succession─the legitimacy of royal blood was easily tested, after all.

55.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_085
55.description: Still, it does beg several questions. Is it right to copy oneself like we would a parchment or a painting? Moreover, is it right to treat such a copy as a tool to hide one's most precious secrets?

56.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_086
56.description: These are questions not easily answered, even by Doga and Unei. Even so, they had a duty to guide their empire through its waning twilight, so they swallowed their doubt and shouldered their fate.

57.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_087
57.description: Even I did not foresee that their clones would prove instrumental in cutting short Xande's wicked ambitions so far in the future. Ah, such a clever scheme as befits my most gifted pupils!

58.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_090
58.description: Hah, Amon! What stories I have of him! So gravely did he treat his research that he never smiled. 'Twould waste precious energy, you see.

59.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_091
59.description: All hint of the dour was washed away, however, when he succeeded in resurrecting Xande. The bliss he felt seemed to pour from his mouth every time he spoke. “Yes, Your Majesty,” “Very good, Your Majesty,” he would chirp, over and over. I can hardly say which was worse.

60.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_092
60.description: He had hung all hopes upon a single man. An emperor, whose revival came at the cost of thousands of lives...

61.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_093
61.description: I have heard tell that in your era, he called himself Fandaniel, the Ascian. Yet I know that regardless of who he pretended to be, he could never hide that nettling persistence of his.

62.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_094
62.description: Even should he suffer a thousand thousand deaths, his soul cleansed by the Lifestream again and again, he would cast aside his life in his search for answers. Such is his nature.

63.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_095
63.description: I never knew him to be any other way. His eyes burned like hot iron, casting about the rotten world before them for the chance to tear it all down and rebuild anew. There were few like him, and doubtless there have been few since.

64.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_100
64.description: Unfortunately, Gancanagh and pachypodium mines are two forms of weaponry that were never developed past the prototype stage before the empire collapsed.

65.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_101
65.description: The intended purpose of the mines was to lie in ambush beneath the soil and take unwary enemies by surprise. Individually they were quite ineffective, but with Gancanagh's leadership, they could be as terrifying as a legion of hardened troops.

66.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_102
66.description: Researchers determined that designing them to resemble plant life would best enable them to blend into their surroundings. Their sensors had to be calibrated as precisely as possible to enable accurate readings from deep underground.

67.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_103
67.description: Alas, they will ever be in a state of imperfection. As they are, they are far from the picture of well-oiled killing machines. One might even say they appear quite charming─until the explosions start, that is.

68.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_110
68.description: After protracted battle and innumerable losses on the southern continent, the empire sought a means by which to use the strength of dragons to aid their conquest.

69.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_111
69.description: The cloning system you encountered was created to make this dream into reality.

70.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_112
70.description: Its genius lies in the unification of two technologies: dragon cloning and control mechanisms for biological organisms. It enabled the creation of winged soldiers whose obedience was absolute.

71.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_113
71.description: The woman in charge of researching and developing the system lost her husband in the southern campaign. It was said that a dragon bit his head clean off, and only his body was returned home for burial.

72.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_114
72.description: She threw herself into her work, so that no others would suffer as she did. “A claw for a claw, a fang for a fang...” Such was her mantra as she spent countless long nights perfecting the system.

73.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_120
73.description: If you include the devastation wrought by her summoning of Bahamut, no wyrm has claimed more Allagan lives than Tiamat.

74.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_121
74.description: The vast plains of the southern continent were so littered with corpses that one could walk for malms without setting foot on the ground. While some could be identified, many more were charred masses of bone and gristle.

75.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_122
75.description: The prospect of cloning such a fierce entity was a daunting one, and I remember hearing that the researchers even made efforts to tone down their subject's innate savagery.

76.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_123
76.description: Tiamat was gifted with considerable skill at manipulating aether. I found the nature of her breath most fascinating. She could concentrate dark aether so intensely that it created aetheric bodies similar to familiars and sprites─something observed in no other dragon.

77.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_124
77.description: It seems they opted not to engineer these talents out of the clones. Whether that was due to the difficulty of doing so or because they hoped to use it to their own advantage, I cannot say...

78.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_130
78.description: Ah, yes, Twintania. The ancient wyvern who held dominion over the wind itself. If I recall, research on cloning the creature was being conducted on the fortieth floor.

79.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_131
79.description: The original Twintania was feared by even the mightiest generals of Allag, and as a child of Bahamut she wrought untold destruction upon her broodsire's enemies. Naturally, she became a subject of much interest after her capture.

80.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_132
80.description: Countless clones of her were produced, and the knowledge gleaned from the process became fundamental to the further development of technology for dragon duplication and control.

81.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_133
81.description: The specimen you encountered was doubtless one of these test subjects, kept there to tighten the shackles of Allag's mastery over dragonkin.

82.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_140
82.description: If a single marvel were to define Allag, it would be the advent of chimerical organisms. So versatile were these creations that researchers would often hold contests to show off their most recent contrivances.

83.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_141
83.description: The chimera as you know it was the culmination of this competitive spirit─a masterpiece that would endure beyond the empire itself. Each iteration brought it closer to perfection, until the third generation combined the strengths of three species of animal into one relentless predator.

84.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_142
84.description: The servomechanical chimera 14X used this deadly organism as its inspiration, and was meant to surpass it in every way─a perfect weapon.

85.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_143
85.description: But if you ask me, all that metal quite takes the art out of the thing! It may be deadly, yes, but there is an allure in organic life that can never be captured by machinery.

86.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_144
86.description: The joining of disparate mundane beasts to make an almost mythical creation was the source of the chimera's grotesque charm. You cannot deliberately forge every part without marring its inherent beauty.

87.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_150
87.description: Ah, I see you found the chimerical laboratory.

88.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_151
88.description: As you may already know, chimerical hybrids evolved over the course of four generations. The first was a blossoming of new life, its potential unrealized. By the fourth generation, chimerical hybrids had achieved a level of intelligence which placed them squarely at the top of the natural order.

89.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_152
89.description: The minotaur belonged to the second generation─simple in composition, yet gifted with the ability to reproduce. The latter characteristic was what set it apart from its more primitive forebears.

90.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_153
90.description: The advantages of a weapon that can multiply quickly and of its own volition are self-evident, I would hope. The minotaur you encountered was enhanced with Allag's most advanced technology, meant to minimize the cost of upkeep while maximizing its combat efficacy.

91.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_160
91.description: The conquest of the southern continent saw Allag contending with eikons, and naturally the researchers of Eureka Orthos were tasked with developing countermeasures in this conflict.

92.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_161
92.description: Now I ask you, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>─what do you think is the most effective way to combat an eikon? Your experience makes you singularly suited to answer such a question.

93.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_162
93.description: The correct answer, of course, is to keep them from being summoned in the first place. By siphoning away the aether that is their lifeblood, one can ensure that the eikons never set foot on solid earth.

94.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_163
94.description: Such was the aeturna's purpose─a beast captured by Xande during an excursion abroad, and possessed of an insatiable hunger for aether.

95.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_164
95.description: It uses that aether not only to feed its own fury, but also to aid its allies in battle. That, combined with the beauty of its form, makes it one of Allag's most elegant weapons─in my humble opinion, of course.

96.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_170
96.description: From the description of your foe, it could be none other than Proto-Kaliya you encountered on the eightieth floor. How curious...

97.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_171
97.description: Work on Kaliya had already been completed, you see. I struggle to find a reason why a prototype would be housed so deep within Eureka Orthos.

98.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_172
98.description: My best guess would be that it served as a base from which to produce a new type of weapon─a divergent species of Kaliya, if you will.

99.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_173
99.description: Your experience seems to bolster that theory, in fact. No Kaliya I know could coordinate with drones and mechanical systems. Whatever its eventual use would have been, it seems Allag's collapse ensured that it will never come to fruition.

100.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_180
100.description: Hmm? A machine that summoned a steel legion of mechanized soldiers and drones?

101.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_181
101.description: Hah hah hah, gods, you are impressive! That would be the Administrator, overseer of Eureka Orthos's defense systems.

102.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_182
102.description: It is no surprise it was housed within the deepmost floors of the facility, as those held its most precious secrets.

103.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_183
103.description: It was designed with the capabilities to fight back an entire enemy army on its own, yet it fell to the might of a single warrior! Hah!

104.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_184
104.description: You are every bit as fierce as I was led to believe, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>! If I am fortunate enough to meet the system's designers again when I return to the aetherial sea, I shall tell them of your triumph! Oh, to see the look on their faces would make this entire reawakening business worth it!

105.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_190
105.description: You wish to hear the tale of Excalibur again? Very well, I see no reason to object─'tis only fitting that you and Koh should know the truth by heart.

106.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_191
106.description: Ahem. Eureka Orthos's supreme eikon created the sword Excalibur from a nigh-bottomless well of aether. The Allagans dubbed it a trigger weapon, which would allow its wielder to summon divine power at will.

107.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_192
107.description: However, it was not to be used for the benefit of Allag's military. It would pierce the heart of the traitor Artorius, breaking his spirit and turning him into the empire's puppet.

108.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_193
108.description: After you brought this broken king low, it appears the sword was separated from his body and placed in safekeeping.

109.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_194
109.description: In time, Eureka Orthos will cease to function, and breathe its final breath deep beneath the earth. When that happens, it shall live on as naught but a legend of a bygone age.

110.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_195
110.description: The name Excalibur appears in another legend, if I recall. Long after the empire was laid to rest, a story was woven of a king of eld who wielded a sword by the same name.

111.name: TEXT_CTSDDD3NOAHTALK_00811_KOHRABNTAH_000_196
111.description: Was this an attempt to glorify the deeds of Artorius, who in the end became little more than a weapon himself? Or perhaps it was an attempt to paint the truth in more palatable shades, transforming atrocity into heroism through the filter of myth. They say that all things give way before time, after all.
